text: Kruskal, Prim, virtual nodes, bottleneck paths.

A spanning tree (生成树) uses n − 1 edges to connect all n nodes; a minimum spanning tree (MST) has the smallest total weight. Kruskal: sort the edges by weight; take an edge if its ends are in different components (union-find, 基础篇第17章), otherwise skip it. Stop after n − 1 edges.
Cut property: for any split of the nodes into two groups, the lightest edge crossing it belongs to some MST.
Kruskal's next edge is always the lightest edge leaving its component, so every taken edge is safe. O(m log m) for the sort.
Check connectivity: if fewer than n − 1 edges were taken, there is no spanning tree (P3366 prints orz). Stopping at n − 1 edges saves time but is not needed for correctness.

Kruskal also builds a minimum spanning forest: stop early when exactly k components remain, and the remaining components are the best k clusters (P1195 口袋的天空). The k − 1 heaviest MST edges cut are the "largest gaps" between clusters.
Prim grows one tree from node 1, always adding the node with the cheapest edge into the tree, exactly like Dijkstra but with d[v] = one edge weight instead of a path length.

The plain O(n²) version is best for dense graphs given as a matrix (m ≈ n²), where sorting all edges for Kruskal would cost more. With a heap it is O(m log n), but on sparse graphs Kruskal is simpler.

Virtual node (超级源点): a cost paid at a node by itself (dig a well, build a power station) becomes an edge from a new node 0. Every field must be connected to water, i.e. to node 0, so the answer is an MST on n + 1 nodes (P1550, CF1245D).
Similar: buying items where a coupon makes item j cheaper after item i (P1194 买礼物) is an MST with a virtual node whose edges cost the full price.

Bottleneck paths: the route between x and y whose smallest edge is as large as possible always runs along the maximum spanning tree (P1967 货车运输). So build that tree once, then answer each query as the minimum edge on a tree path, with binary lifting as in 第9章(low[u][k] next to up[u][k]). The minimum spanning tree likewise minimises the largest edge (P1396 营救).
The graph may be disconnected: run the DFS from every unvisited node, keep a component id, and answer −1 across components. Node 0 is the sentinel above every root, so its low[] must be +∞.
Swap one edge; largest and strict second largest on a path.

The second-best spanning tree (次小生成树): every other spanning tree is reached from the MST by adding one non-tree edge (u, v, w) and removing an edge on the tree path u–v. To keep the total as small as possible, remove the largest path edge: new total = MST − max + w.

For the strict second-best (P4180), the result must be larger than the MST. If w equals the path maximum, remove the largest path edge that is strictly smaller than w instead. So each binary-lifting jump stores the largest and the strictly second-largest edge.

MST = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10. Edge 3–4 (w = 3) closes the cycle 3–1–2–4 whose edges are 2, 1, 3: the largest equals w, so swap out the strict second, 2: 10 − 2 + 3 = 11. Edge 4–5 (w = 6) gives 10 − 4 + 6 = 12. Answer 11.
Merging two (largest, second) pairs must keep the second strictly smaller: the add helper ignores a value equal to the current largest. Weights are non-negative here, so −1 can mean "none".
